title: Chow's lemma for separated morphisms of finite type over a qcqs base
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $f:X\to S$ a separated morphism of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then there exist an integer $n\ge0$, a scheme $X'$, a morphism $\pi:X'\to X$ that is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and an immersion $j:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] into the projective space $\mathbf P^n_S=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] such that $p\circ j=f\circ\pi$, where $p:\mathbf P^n_S\to S$ is the projection.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071) and its proof (Proposition 01ZJ, Proposition 01ZA, Lemma 01ZM descend-finite-presentation, Lemma 01ZQ descend-separated-finite-presentation, Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 0200 coherent-lemma-chow-Noetherian)

proof.text: *A finitely presented envelope.* Since $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f$ is separated and of finite type, Stacks Proposition 01ZJ [prop-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp] (applied to the envelope $\mathsf{Env}_{\mathrm{fp}}(X/S)=(X^{\mathrm{fp}},i^{\mathrm{fp}}_{X/S})$ of [def-nagata-finite-type-closed-in-fp]; Lean: Scheme.Hom.exists_isClosedImmersion_isSeparated_locallyOfFinitePresentation, closed) gives a scheme $Y=X^{\mathrm{fp}}$, a closed immersion $i:X\to Y$ and a morphism $g:Y\to S$ which is separated and of finite presentation, with $g\circ i=f$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, first paragraph, first sentence (Proposition 01ZJ, separated-closed-in-finite-presentation)

proof.text: *It suffices to treat $g$.* Suppose $n\ge0$, a scheme $Y'$, a proper surjective $\pi_Y:Y'\to Y$ and an immersion $j_Y:Y'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ with $p\circ j_Y=g\circ\pi_Y$ are found. Put $X'=Y'\times_YX$ (fibre product of $\pi_Y$ and $i$ [def-pc-fibre-product]) with projections $e:X'\to Y'$ and $\pi:X'\to X$, so $\pi_Y\circ e=i\circ\pi$. Then $\pi$ is proper, as a base change of the proper $\pi_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), and surjective, as a base change of the surjective $\pi_Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. The projection $e$ is a closed immersion, as a base change of the closed immersion $i$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], hence an immersion (a closed immersion followed by the identity, an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]); so $j=j_Y\circ e:X'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ is an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). Finally $p\circ j=g\circ\pi_Y\circ e=g\circ i\circ\pi=f\circ\pi$. So $(n,X',\pi,j)$ is as claimed for $f$. It remains to prove the lemma for $g:Y\to S$, separated and of finite presentation.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, first paragraph, 'Clearly, if we prove the assertion for $Y$, then the result follows for $X$' (written out by the agent)

proof.text: *Noetherian approximation of $S$.* By [prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] (Stacks Proposition 01ZA; Lean closed) $S$ admits a Noetherian approximation [def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system]: a small cofiltered diagram of schemes of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with affine transition morphisms and a limit cone with vertex $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] it is re-indexed by a nonempty directed set $J$: an inverse system $(S_j)_{j\in J}$ of schemes of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with affine transition morphisms $s_{j'j}:S_{j'}\to S_j$ ($j'\ge j$) [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and projections $q_j:S\to S_j$ exhibiting $S=\varprojlim_jS_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Each $S_j$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence quasi-compact and, being locally Noetherian, quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, second paragraph, first sentence (Proposition 01ZA, proposition-approximate)

proof.text: *Descending $Y$.* Since $g$ is of finite presentation and the $S_j$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated with affine transition morphisms, [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1) (Stacks Lemma 01ZM; source repository: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.exists_isPullback_of_finitePresentation, sorry-free) gives $j_0\in J$, a morphism of finite presentation $g_{j_0}:Y_{j_0}\to S_{j_0}$ and an isomorphism $Y\cong Y_{j_0}\times_{S_{j_0}}S$ over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. As $g_{j_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $S_{j_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $Y_{j_0}$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). For $j\ge j_0$ put $Y_j=Y_{j_0}\times_{S_{j_0}}S_j$ with projection $g_j:Y_j\to S_j$; $g_j$ is of finite presentation, a base change of $g_{j_0}$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3), and $Y\cong Y_j\times_{S_j}S$ over $S$ (transitivity of fibre products).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, second paragraph, second sentence (Lemma 01ZM, descend-finite-presentation)

proof.text: *Making the model separated.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-separated] (Stacks Lemma 01ZQ) to the system $(S_j)_{j\in J}$ with $0=j_0$, $X_0=Y_{j_0}$, $Y_0=S_{j_0}$ and $f_0=g_{j_0}$: $S_{j_0}$ and $Y_{j_0}$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (steps 3, 4); for $j\ge j_0$ the base change of $f_0$ to $S_j$ is $g_j:Y_j\to S_{j_0}\times_{S_{j_0}}S_j=S_j$, and its base change to $S$ is $Y_{j_0}\times_{S_{j_0}}S\to S$, which is isomorphic over $S$ to the separated $g$ (step 4), hence separated (separatedness is invariant under isomorphism over $S$: the diagonals correspond under the isomorphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]). So there is $j_1\ge j_0$ with $g_{j_1}:Y_{j_1}\to S_{j_1}$ separated; it is of finite presentation (step 4), and $Y\cong Y_{j_1}\times_{S_{j_1}}S$ over $S$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, second paragraph, third sentence (Lemma 01ZQ, descend-separated-finite-presentation)

proof.text: *Chow's lemma over the Noetherian stage.* $S_{j_1}$ is Noetherian (step 3) and $g_{j_1}$ is separated and of finite type (finite presentation implies locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). By [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200; only its first assertion is used) there are $n\ge0$, a scheme $Y'_{j_1}$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi_{j_1}:Y'_{j_1}\to Y_{j_1}$ and an immersion $\iota:Y'_{j_1}\to\mathbf P^n_{S_{j_1}}=S_{j_1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] with $p_{j_1}\circ\iota=g_{j_1}\circ\pi_{j_1}$, $p_{j_1}$ the projection to $S_{j_1}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0202 (lemma-chow-finite-type, line 3071), proof, second paragraph, last two sentences (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0200, coherent-lemma-chow-Noetherian)

proof.text: *Base change back to $S$.* Write $T\mapsto T_S=T\times_{S_{j_1}}S$ for base change along $q_{j_1}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $Y'=(Y'_{j_1})_S$. The morphism $(\pi_{j_1})_S:Y'\to(Y_{j_1})_S$ is identified, by pasting of fibre squares, with the projection $Y'_{j_1}\times_{Y_{j_1}}(Y_{j_1})_S\to(Y_{j_1})_S$, a base change of $\pi_{j_1}$; so it is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b) and surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Composing with the isomorphism $(Y_{j_1})_S\cong Y$ over $S$ of step 5 (an isomorphism is a closed immersion, hence proper (c), and bijective) gives $\pi_Y:Y'\to Y$, proper (a) and surjective. Likewise, since $Y'_{j_1}\to S_{j_1}$ factors as $p_{j_1}\circ\iota$, the morphism $\iota_S:Y'\to(\mathbf P^n_{S_{j_1}})_S$ is identified with the projection $Y'_{j_1}\times_{\mathbf P^n_{S_{j_1}}}(\mathbf P^n_{S_{j_1}})_S\to(\mathbf P^n_{S_{j_1}})_S$, a base change of the immersion $\iota$, hence an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (1). Transitivity of fibre products gives an isomorphism over $S$, $(\mathbf P^n_{S_{j_1}})_S=(S_{j_1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z})\times_{S_{j_1}}S\cong S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}=\mathbf P^n_S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]; an isomorphism is an immersion (a closed immersion followed by the identity [def-weil-closed-immersion]), so the composite $j_Y:Y'\to\mathbf P^n_S$ is an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (e). All the identifications are over $S$, and $p_{j_1}\circ\iota=g_{j_1}\circ\pi_{j_1}$ base changes to the equality of the two structure morphisms $Y'\to S$; hence $p\circ j_Y=g\circ\pi_Y$. This is the lemma for $g$, and by step 2 for $f$.
